beats.narration: Professional investors had sold more shares of one company than were actually available to trade.
The company was GameStop, a mall video game store that most of Wall Street assumed was dying.
Hedge funds borrowed its shares and sold them, planning to buy them back later, for less.
By January, shares sold short had passed a hundred and forty percent of the available float.
On a Reddit forum called WallStreetBets, ordinary traders did the math.
If they kept buying, the short sellers would be forced to buy too, at any price.
So they bought. Under twenty dollars a share in early January. Three hundred and forty-seven by the twenty-seventh.
Melvin Capital, one of the biggest short sellers, lost more than half its money that month.
The next morning, Robinhood and other brokers stopped letting customers buy.
The price crashed. Within weeks, Congress was holding hearings.
Sell more shares than anyone can buy back, and sooner or later, someone asks for them.
